title: Finite-stalk specialization criterion for local constancy
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose every geometric stalk $G_{\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is finite as a set, and for every geometric point $\bar s$ and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the specialization map $G_{\bar s}\to G_{\bar t}$ is bijective. Here specialization is induced by restriction of pointed etale neighbourhood germs through $S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. Then $G$ is finite locally constant: there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to S\}$ and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-constructible-locally-constant].

source.place: Tag 0GKC, label lemma-characterize-locally-constant-module, (2) implies (1), finite coefficient ring and Noetherian base

proof.text: At each point choose its algebraically closed geometric point and its finite stalk M. Lift the identity of M to a linear section map f on a pointed etale neighbourhood U.

Let E be the locus where the section map induces a bijection on a canonical geometric stalk. Specialization invariance also identifies all geometric points above the same ordinary point, so E is stable under specialization in both directions and contains the chosen point.

Choose an affine open through the point of U. Its morphism to S is locally of finite type, so it is locally Noetherian and affine quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Its components are finite and the scheme is quasi-sober. The topological neighborhood lemma gives an open through the point contained in E.

Restrict the section map to this open W. The original germ formula for restriction and specialization invariance show it is bijective on every geometric stalk of W. The constant-sheaf adjunction and stalk detection therefore give a trivialization with finite module M.

Choose W at every ordinary point of S. Their maps are etale and hit their indexing points, hence give a jointly surjective etale cover and the required finite trivializations. The index set is empty when S is empty.
